title: wsutils: add a local implementation of g_memdup2

notes.body:
Can you please use `g_memdup2` instead and copy the function from GLib?

Besides not requiring memorizing a new exception with `ws_memdup` it will actually fix the integer overflow issue for all Wireshark builds. This patch unfixes all Wireshark builds for all GLib versions, past and future.

We need to check if it exists at compile time using CMake and link in `g_memdup2` otherwise.

> Can you please use `g_memdup2` instead and copy the function from GLib?

Do you mean to import a local copy of the implementation?
I pushed a new version. I hope it addresses your point.

That's what I meant, import a local copy, since it is such a trivial function. You could keep the `ws_memdup` name, as long as the signature is the same as `g_memdup2` (using `gsize`), but I personally would prefer not, it's just one more exception to have to remember.

@crondaemon So you need to use `gpointer ws_memdup(gconstpointer mem, gsize byte_size)` (note the `gsize` instead of `guint`). The point of having a `g_memdup2` in the first place is to avoid possibly narrowing a `gsize` into a `guint`.

But my suggestion is to use g_memdup2 instead of ws_memdup. We can supply our own implementation of g_memdup2 for older GLib versions. Does that work for you?
It does. Pushed a new version.
We used to have various glib compatibility functions. Look at how that was done.
Can you point me to one? For checking.

I stuck because linking fails here. I may need to add wsutils somewhere. Can you help me here? I am missing something.
You need to add the `extern "C"` linkage specifier with the `#ifdef __cplusplus` guards.

> You need to add the `extern "C"` linkage specifier with the `#ifdef __cplusplus` guards.

...and do so *after* including glib.h, otherwise Weird Things Happen because GLib's headers appear to include at least one C++ header file in newer versions of GLib.

+/*
+* Provide some functions that are not present in older
+* GLIB versions (down to 2.22)
+*
+* Wireshark - Network traffic analyzer
+* By Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>
+* Copyright 1998 Gerald Combs
+*
+* SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+*/
+#include "config.h"
+
+#include <glib.h>
+
+#include "glib-compat.h"
+#if !GLIB_CHECK_VERSION(2, 68, 0)
+/**
+* g_memdup2:
+* mem: the memory to copy
+* byte_size: the number of bytes to copy.
+*
+* Allocates byte_size bytes of memory, and copies byte_size bytes into it from mem . If mem is NULL it returns NULL.
+*
+* This replaces g_memdup(), which was prone to integer overflows when converting the argument from a gsize to a guint.
+*
+* Since: 2.68
+**/
+gpointer
+g_memdup2(gconstpointer mem, gsize byte_size)
+{
+  gpointer new_mem;
+
+  if (mem && byte_size != 0) {
+      new_mem = g_malloc(byte_size);
+      memcpy(new_mem, mem, byte_size);
+  }
+  else
+    new_mem = NULL;
+
+  return new_mem;
+}
+#endif

commits_data.message:
wsutils: add local implementation of g_memdup2.

g_memdup() was deprecated and replaced with g_memdup2() in GLib 2.68,
we provide our own copy of g_memdup2() for older GLib versions.
